title: Those who hear and do not choke the word are led to faith
source_text: XII. Itaque juxta ipsum, quicunque verbum audiunt, neque aspernantur consilium Dei in semetipsos, ac verbum Dei non suffocant curis aut divitiis, aut voluptatibus hujus vitae, ii, inquam, Dei opem & operam sentiunt, ejusque gratuita benevolentia ad fidem & vitam deducuntur. Qui vero contra faciunt, suae negligentiae & contumaciae imputare debent, quod a Deo fide non donentur.
pass_a_gloss: XII. And so according to him, whoever hear the word, and do not spurn the counsel of God against themselves, and do not choke the word of God with cares or riches, or pleasures of this life, they, I say, feel the help & work of God, & by his gratuitous benevolence are led to faith & life. But those who do the contrary, must impute it to their own negligence & contumacy, that they are not gifted by God with faith.
pass_b_english: Thesis XII. According to him, then, all who hear the word, do not reject God's counsel against themselves, and do not smother God's word with the worries, riches or pleasures of this life experience God's help and working, and are brought to faith and life by his free goodwill.
Those who act otherwise must lay it to their own carelessness and defiance that God does not give them faith.
